statement: For a time-homogeneous nearest-neighbor Markov chain in a fixed environment and nonzero l, if q(x)=P_x(lim_n X_n·l=+infinity) has inf_x q(x)>0, then q(x)=1 for all x.
assumptions: A_l is unchanged by deleting a finite prefix
proof_or_counterexample: For each start x, the Markov property and finite-prefix invariance give E_x[1_{A_l}|F_n]=q(X_n). Martingale convergence to E_x[1_{A_l}|F_infinity]=1_{A_l} and q(X_n)>=c>0 force 1_{A_l}=1 a.s. The result holds for every x separately.

remaining_gap: Neither iid nor ellipticity has been shown to imply inf_x q(x)>0; this does not settle C0044.

statement: For d>=3 and 0<kappa<1/(2d), the deterministic environment with outward e1 transition p=1-(2d-1)kappa, inward q=kappa, transverse transitions kappa, and symmetric e1 transitions at level zero has 0<P_x(A_+)<1 for every x, with inf_x P_x(A_+)=inf_x P_x(A_-)=0 and P_x(A_+ union A_-)=1.
assumptions: fixed layered deterministic environment, not iid
proof_or_counterexample: Set c=p+q and r=q/p<1. Embedded first-coordinate jumps have outward probability p/c, inward q/c, and from zero symmetric signs. Every excursion from zero has return probability r, so there are finitely many returns a.s.; the final outward-biased half-line excursion diverges. By hitting probability r^|k| and symmetry, h(k)=1-r^k/2 for k>=0, h(k)=r^{-k}/2 for k<=0. At k=0, c/2>=kappa exactly when kappa<=1/(2d). Thus the transition rows are uniformly kappa-elliptic and the displayed event probabilities have the stated infima.
